DEFINITION · qeva:1:proof@1

Proof

A proof is a finite, checkable chain from admitted premises to a conclusion under declared rules.

editoriallogic · proof
Trace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

A proof is a finite, checkable chain from admitted premises to a conclusion under declared rules.

EXACT

The compact statement

An S-proof of P from Γ is a finite sequence of formulas ending in P, each of which is an axiom, an admitted premise, or follows from earlier formulas by an S-rule.

Example

A two-line derivation may use P and P→Q to conclude Q by modus ponens.

Boundary / caveat

A persuasive explanation and a formal derivation serve different purposes; QEVA can link both without calling them identical.

Assumptions

  • The declared formal proof system context is fixed.
